note: Made by Obay's second method (see "method"): the chapter is split into sections that each carry one deep meaning, 10 picture ideas are written for each ("sections"), the top two for each picture are made and the better is chosen by eye. Each scene is made wide (1920x1088) and tall (1088x1920) from the same description and starts at the first word of its verse, or at its "from" words inside the verse. Pictures already used in the chapters beside this one are not repeated, and the important part of every picture sits in the upper two thirds, clear of the words.
method: Second method, asked for by Obay on 2026-11-21 after the sentence-by-sentence pictures did not connect: (1) split the chapter into sections that each carry one deep meaning, written as one plain sentence; (2) write 10 different picture ideas for each section; (3) judge them: which shows the deep meaning most truly, then which a watcher understands at once while hearing the words, then which is most engaging; (4) make the top two for each picture slot as real pictures ("candidates") and choose by eye. A section has one or two pictures. What he said went wrong before: he could not tell why some pictures were there, could not connect them to the meaning, and some were too abstract.

sections.meaning: Do not believe everything that sounds spiritual: test it. What is from God owns that Jesus Christ really came, in the flesh.
ideas: A man taps the lake ice with a pole before anyone steps onto it
A climber pulls hard on the rope to test the anchor before she trusts her weight to it
A mother tests the baby's milk on her wrist
A jeweller studies a ring through his glass
A carpenter presses his thumb into a beam to check it for rot
An electrician tests a wire before he touches it
A newborn is laid in its mother's arms, real and warm
At the arrivals gate a mother holds her grown son's face in both hands: he is really here
A violinist tunes to the one true note of a tuning fork
Friends crowd round someone back from far away and take hold of his shoulders

sections.meaning: You belong to God and have overcome, because the one in you is greater than the one in the world. Whom you listen to shows where you belong.
ideas: A family sits warm by the fire while a blizzard beats on the window
A woman carries a lantern through a storm and its flame burns steady
A young tree bends in a gale and holds by its roots
A small boat rides out heavy waves
A small boy walks calmly past a big barking dog
In a noisy crowd a little girl turns, her face lighting up, at her mother's voice
A crowd gathers round a loud showman while a few sit listening to a quiet old teacher
A dog pricks up its ears at its owner's whistle among many people
Half a class leans in to the teacher, half turns to the boy clowning at the back
A helmsman strains to hear the captain over the storm

sections.meaning: Love comes from God, because God is love. He showed it by sending his only Son so that we might live: he loved us first.
ideas: A mother scoops up her crying toddler who has fallen off his bicycle
An old man feeds his frail wife with a spoon, both of them smiling
Sunlight pours through a window onto a mother rocking her baby
People on a bench turn their faces to the first warm sun after winter
A spring rises among rocks and children drink from the stream it feeds
A father sees off his son, a rescue worker, beside the truck that will take him into the flood
A man gives blood, and the line runs to the patient in the next bed
A lifeboat crew launches into heavy seas while an old father watches from the pier
A father kneels with open arms behind a sulking boy who has turned his back
A hand reaches down and pulls a man up over a cliff edge

sections.meaning: Since God loved us like this, we must love one another. No one has seen God, but when we love one another he lives in us and his love is seen.
ideas: Friends carry a man in his wheelchair up the steps together, all of them laughing
A whole neighbourhood raises the wall of a new house for a family
A line of people passes sandbags from hand to hand
Teenagers clear an old man's path of snow while he watches from the window
A woman brings soup to a sick neighbour
Young people serve a meal to old people who live alone
A child flies a kite: the wind is not seen, only what it lifts
A man teaches his neighbour's daughter to ride a bicycle
Neighbours rebuild a barn after a fire
Strangers push a stalled car out of the rain

sections.meaning: We know that God lives in us and we in him: he gave us his Spirit, and we have seen that the Father sent the Son to save the world. Whoever stays in love stays in God.
ideas: On the quay a rescued fisherman in a blanket points back to the lifeboatman who pulled him out
A ring is slipped onto a finger at a wedding
A lit window on a dark night: someone lives here
A father puts his own watch on his son's wrist
A baby sleeps in a sling against its mother as she walks through a busy market
A girl nestles in her grandfather's lap in a sunlit armchair while he reads to her
A whole family squeezes onto one sofa under one blanket, laughing
A child floats on her back in the water, held up by her father's hands
A tired traveller sinks into his own armchair at home
An old couple sit close on a porch swing

sections.meaning: Love that has done its full work makes us bold for the day of judgment. There is no fear in love: complete love throws fear out.
ideas: A small girl leaps from the pool's edge into her father's waiting arms, laughing
A child is tossed high in the air and laughs, sure of the hands below
A frightened rescue dog comes out from under the bed and leans into a child's arms
A toddler takes his first steps toward open arms
A girl walks into a dark room holding her father's hand
A boy walks smiling into the judge's room: the judge is his father
A child sleeps through a thunderstorm
A girl stands at the top of the high slide and lets go
A shy boy sings out in the school play when he finds his mother's face in the crowd
A night light glows beside a sleeping child

sections.meaning: We love because he loved us first. No one can love the God he has not seen while hating the brother he has seen.
ideas: A father hands his son an ice cream, and the boy at once holds it out to his little sister
A grandmother braids her daughter's hair while the daughter braids her own little girl's
A mother kisses her daughter's head as the daughter rocks her baby brother
The moon shines because the sun shines on it
Two brothers who had quarrelled embrace at the door
A man sits at a full table while his brother waits outside in the rain
A boy who has just been helped up turns to help the next child up
A girl wraps her little brother in the towel her mother has just wrapped round her
A man shares his umbrella with the brother he had been avoiding
A child given two sweets passes one on

candidates.prompt: On a frozen lake in clear winter daylight a man in a heavy coat crouches at the shore and strikes the ice hard with a long wooden pole, watching it closely, testing whether it will hold. Behind him three friends with skates over their shoulders wait on the bank and do not step out yet.

At the top of a rock face in bright daylight a woman climber in a helmet and harness pulls hard with both hands on the rope fixed to its anchor, leaning back and watching the anchor closely, testing it before she trusts her weight to it. The drop behind her is clear but she is safely on the ledge.

In a bright hospital room a newborn baby, wrapped in a white blanket, has just been laid in its mother's arms. She looks down at the tiny face in wonder and touches the baby's cheek with one finger, and the baby's small hand grips the father's finger. Real, warm and close. Soft daylight from the window.

At an airport arrivals gate a mother in her sixties holds her grown son's face in both her hands, looking into his eyes with tears and a wide smile: he is really here, in person, after a long time away. He is smiling, a bag still on his shoulder. Other travellers pass softly out of focus behind them. Bright daylight through tall windows.

Inside a small house at night a family of four sits close together on a rug by a bright wood fire, warm, calm and smiling, the children leaning on their parents. Through the big window beside them a fierce blizzard rages in the dark, snow driving hard against the glass. The warm firelight fills the room; the storm stays outside.

A woman in a rain jacket walks steadily up a hill path at night through a fierce storm of wind and rain, holding up a glass storm lantern. The flame inside the lantern burns bright and perfectly steady, lighting her calm face, while trees bend and rain streaks all around her.

In a crowded, noisy fairground in daylight, full of people moving in every direction, a little girl of about five has turned right round toward us, her face lighting up with recognition and joy: she has heard her mother's voice. Her mother is seen only as an outstretched hand at the near edge of the frame. The crowd behind the girl is a blur; she is sharp.

In a town square in daylight a big crowd presses round a loud showman in a bright suit who shouts through a megaphone from a little stage. In the foreground, apart from the crowd, three people sit on a low wall listening closely and gladly to a quiet old man who talks to them with an open hand. The showman and his crowd fill the background; the small quiet group is nearer and sharper.

On a park path in bright daylight a mother has dropped to her knees and scooped up her crying toddler, who has just fallen off his little bicycle. She holds him tight against her and kisses the top of his head; his arms are round her neck. The small bicycle lies on its side on the path behind them.

In a sunlit room an old man sits close beside his frail, white-haired wife in her armchair and feeds her gently with a spoon from a bowl, his other hand steadying her chin with great tenderness. They are both smiling into each other's eyes. Warm clear daylight from a window falls on them both.

Beside a rescue truck with its back doors open, an older father grips the shoulders of his grown son, who wears a rescue worker's helmet and bright jacket and carries a medical pack. The father looks into his son's face with love and pain, letting him go. In the distance behind them a flooded town lies under heavy grey cloud, where the son is being sent to save lives.

In a hospital room two beds stand side by side. In one, a healthy man lies with his sleeve rolled up, giving blood; a thin tube runs from his arm across to the pale patient in the other bed, who is beginning to open her eyes. The donor has turned his head to watch her with a quiet smile. Clean bright daylight.

At the foot of a wide flight of stone steps in bright daylight, four friends lift a young man in his wheelchair and carry him up the steps together, one at each corner, all of them laughing, the man in the chair laughing most of all with his arms spread wide.

On a building plot in bright morning light, a dozen neighbours of all ages push up the timber frame of a house wall together with their hands and with poles, straining and smiling. A young family, the parents and two small children, stands to one side watching with grateful, amazed faces: the house is for them.

On a harbour quay in grey morning light a soaked fisherman wrapped in a blanket points back with his whole arm at a lifeboat crewman in orange oilskins who is coiling a rope beside the lifeboat. The fisherman is telling a small group of townspeople how that man pulled him out of the sea; they look from him to the crewman with wonder.

A close view at an outdoor wedding in soft daylight: a man's hands slide a plain gold ring onto a woman's finger. Her other hand rests over his. Both of their smiling faces are seen above, a little out of focus, looking down at the ring.

In a big old armchair by a sunny window a grandfather reads from a picture book to his small granddaughter, who is nestled deep in his lap, leaning back against his chest with her head under his chin, completely at home. His arm is round her. Warm clear daylight falls on them both.

A whole family, grandparents, parents and three children, is squeezed together onto one sofa under one big blanket on a rainy afternoon, leaning on one another and laughing. Rain runs down the window behind them. Warm lamplight on their faces.

At an outdoor swimming pool in bright sunshine a small girl of about four in a swimsuit and armbands is in mid-air, leaping from the pool's edge with her arms flung wide and a huge fearless laugh, toward her father's two arms reaching up for her from the water. The father is seen only as arms, shoulders and the back of his head, low in the water.

In a child's bedroom in soft daylight a thin, timid rescue dog has crept out from under the bed and leans its whole body into the arms of a boy of about eight who sits on the floor, hugging it gently with his cheek on its head. The dog's eyes are half closed; its fear is gone. The dark space under the bed is behind them.

At a park in bright summer daylight a father's arm, at the edge of the frame, has just handed an ice-cream cone to his son of about seven. The boy has at once turned and holds the cone out to his little sister of about three, offering her the first lick, with a proud, kind smile. She reaches for it with both hands, delighted.

On the wooden steps of a porch in warm daylight three generations sit one behind another: a grandmother braids her grown daughter's hair, and the daughter at the same moment braids the hair of her own little girl, who sits on the step below hugging a doll. All three are smiling. Seen a little from the side so that the row of three is clear.
